Their argument rests on a two-moment certificate — the trace and the Frobenius norm of the Weil–Gabor compression, read against block structure and integrality — and that certificate is provably exhausted: within the data class (tr, Frobenius, positive-index count, integer atoms) an on-line double and a shallow off-line pair are indistinguishable, which pins the distinct-zeros optimum at $N_{d}/N = 5/6$ and the simple fraction at $2/3$. A natural proposal to break this degeneracy is to adjoin, at a second bandwidth $\lambda' = 1/2 + o(1)$ inside the Rudnick–Sarnak range, the unconditionally computable signed third trace together with two spectral-capacity rows: an all-$V$ eigenvalue-count ladder and a garnish-capacity fuzz row. This paper proves, at the model level, and certifies computationally, that the augmentation adds exactly nothing. The marginal value of the entire cubic block over the two-moment baseline is $\delta_0 = 0$ identically, an exact LP equality with an explicit, hand-checkable witness law. It holds over the full adversary grid for the distinct-zeros benchmark ($940$ records, $|\delta_0| < 10^{-12}$ everywhere, corner $5/6$); for the simple-fraction benchmark (corner $2/3$) at its two decision cells together with cross-checks, converged clean at the stopping criterion; and inside the near-CUE data class licensed by the unconditional pair-correlation theorem of Baluyot–Goldston–Suriajaya–Turnage-Butterbaugh, where the absorption is by strict slack: there the cubic row does not bind. The structural explanation is a set of exact identities proved here. On isolated blocks the signed cubic row is the affine function $3F - 2$ of the Frobenius row plus the second integrality level, hence blind to doubles-versus-pairs at every depth. On the $\psi_1$-zero grid the bandwidth-one Frobenius row degenerates exactly to the multiplicity count while the half-bandwidth kernel stays position-sensitive, so the cubic budget is met by arrangement at zero cost. Spectral escape is capped sharply at $2\sqrt{2}\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{led}} \varepsilon_g}\,N = o(N)$, and a scalar cubic tail row with any divergent cutoff is unconditionally vacuous. The pair-interference channel, the one gap in the atom-only model theorem, is closed by an integrality theorem throughout the admissible pair-depth family ($w \le 1$, plus deep probes at $w \in \{1.5, 2\}$): proved unconditionally for single-pair columns to $w \le 2.8$, which covers that whole family, and for multi-pair columns at $w \le 0.82$ ($w \le 0.98$ modulo one crowding cap whose ledger constant is interval-certified; on the deepest sliver $w \in (0.98, 1]$ the coverage is adversarial-numerical with the unconditional $8/9$ backstop), with an unconditional $8/9$-strength spectral backstop at all depths. Mixed-depth multi-pair columns involving the deep probes $w \in \{1.5, 2\}$ rest on that backstop together with converged adversarial pricing. The two-moment certificate, and with it the bandwidth-one ceiling, is robust under Rudnick–Sarnak-range cubic augmentation with capacity control.

papers.title: The volume of foliated surfaces with geometric genus one
papers.abstract: We prove the sharp volume bound $\mathrm{vol}(\mathcal{F})\ge 1/6$ for complex foliated surfaces of general type with positive geometric genus. We also study the equality case and apply the bound to the algebraic integrability and finiteness of small volumes on irregular surfaces.

papers.title: The Watermark and Double Ladder Theorems: the discriminant group of the Néron–Severi lattice of a Fermat surface of prime degree
papers.abstract: Let $S_m\subset\mathbb{P}^3$ be the complex Fermat surface $x_0^m+x_1^m+x_2^m+x_3^m=0$ of prime degree $m\ge 5$. Its Néron–Severi lattice $\mathrm{NS}(S_m)$ is generated by the classes of the $3m^2$ lines on $S_m$ (Schütt–Shioda–van Luijk, Degtyarev). We prove that $|\mathrm{disc}\,\mathrm{NS}(S_m)| = m^{3(m-3)^2}$ (the Watermark Theorem), which answers, for prime degree, the determinant question asked by Shioda in 1987, and we determine the discriminant group itself: $\mathrm{NS}(S_m)^*/\mathrm{NS}(S_m)\cong(\mathbb{Z}/m)^{3m^2-24m+59}\times(\mathbb{Z}/m^2)^{3m-16}$ for $m\ge 7$, and $(\mathbb{Z}/5)^{10}\times\mathbb{Z}/25$ for $m=5$ (the Double Ladder Theorem). The transcendental lattice of $S_m$ has the same discriminant group. Both proofs work with the explicit integer intersection matrix $G$ of the lines and use only elementary lattice arithmetic: the action of $G$ on functions pulled back along the $m+1$ pencils of directions of $(\mathbb{Z}/m)^2$, an explicit sublattice of $\ker G$ of index $m^{12}$, and two index computations for the order; an integer identity $GYG=6m^2G$ for the exponent, and a factorization of $G$ modulo $m$ through twelve one-variable "shadows" for the number of cyclic factors of order $m^2$. The lattice statements of both theorems are checked in the proof assistant Lean 4 with the Mathlib library, with no axiom beyond the three standard ones; the identification of $G$ with the intersection matrix of the lines is proved by hand and checked by computer. This work has not been refereed by a human expert.

papers.title: Topological recursion for spin enumeration of hypermaps
papers.abstract:
We establish topological recursion for the spin enumeration of hypermaps, or, in the dual language, spin dessins d'enfants. This problem has remarkable features distinguishing it from other applications of topological recursion to enumerative combinatorics. First, the spectral curve is elliptic rather than rational, as in most cases studied before. Second, it contains degenerate ramification points, and one has to apply a version of degenerate topological recursion. Finally, the meromorphic correlator differentials have "moving" poles on the antidiagonals between pairs of distinct arguments, and one has to adjust the loop equations to this kind of degeneracy as well.
  The computations involve concepts of different kinds, such as BKP integrability, Gaussian integrals, the x-y swap, and symplectic duality.

papers.title: Topology-Aware Representation Alignment for Semi-Supervised Vision-Language Learning
papers.abstract: Vision-language models have shown strong performance, but they often generalize poorly to specialized domains. While semi-supervised vision-language learning mitigates this limitation by leveraging a small set of labeled image-text pairs together with abundant unlabeled images, existing methods remain fundamentally pairwise and fail to model the global structure of multimodal representation manifolds. Most existing topology-based alignment methods rely on persistence diagram matching, which neither guarantees geometric alignment nor uses the image-text pairing information central to vision-language learning. We propose Topology-Aware Representation Alignment for Semi-Supervised Vision-Language Learning (ToMA), a framework that uses persistent homology to decompose pairwise relations into $H_0$-death and $H_1$-birth relations and aligns them across modalities through available cross-modal correspondences. This lightweight decomposition captures both connectivity and cycle-closing structure without constructing 2-simplices. Experiments show clear improvements on remote sensing, while fashion results reveal strong gains in classification and particularly strong retrieval improvements for difficult queries. Additional analysis shows that ToMA provides more consistent gains than alternative topology-based objectives and that lightweight $H_1$-birth edges provide useful higher-order structural signals.

papers.title: Two non-semisimple quantum invariants of lens spaces
papers.abstract: We calculate the chromatic spherical invariant $\mathscr{K}_{\mathrm{Rep}(H)}(L(p,q))$ of lens spaces $L(p, q)$ for arbitrary finite-dimensional unibalanced, unimodular Hopf algebras $H$. In the case of the index-2 Nichols Hopf algebra $\mathcal{K}_2$ and $q=1$, we find that the invariant of $L(p, 1)$ depends only on the parity of $p$ for $p\geq 1$. We also describe the duals $\mathcal{S_I}(M)^*$ of the admissible skein modules of handlebodies $M=H_g$ and of $M=L(p, q)$ for arbitrary tensor ideals $\mathcal{I}$ of a ribbon tensor category. In particular, $\mathcal{S_I}(L(p, q))^*$ corresponds with cyclic traces on $\mathcal{I}$ satisfying a property reminiscent of the modified trace condition.

papers.title: Uniform non-homogeneous vector bundles: A counterexample to the conjecture of Dr\'ezet and Ballico-Ellia
papers.abstract: We construct a rank-9 uniform non-homogeneous vector bundle on ${\mathbb P}^5$. This yields the first counterexample to the longstanding open conjecture that every uniform vector bundle of rank $r<2n$ on ${\mathbb P}^n$ is homogeneous.

papers.title: Unipotent tensor categories and pronilpotent Lie quasibialgebras
papers.abstract: We construct a bijection between tensor equivalence classes of unipotent tensor categories over $\C$ and continuous Lie quasibialgebras with linearly compact pronilpotent underlying Lie algebra, modulo continuous isomorphisms and classical twists. The bijection is defined using a fixed universal quantization functor and solves the problem raised in Remark~4.6 of arXiv:0708.1487 by Etingof and Gelaki. The proof combines reconstruction with filtered dequantization modulo twists and convergence of universal formulas. A category admits a tensor fiber functor precisely when a classical twist removes its curvature.

papers.title: Uniqueness of twisted linear periods over Archimedean division algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\DD$ be $\R$, $\C$, or $\HH$, and let $H=\GL_p(\DD)\times\GL_q(\DD)$ be the block diagonal subgroup of $G=\GL_{p+q}(\DD)$. We prove that $\dim\Hom_H(\pi,\eta)\leq1$ for every irreducible Casselman--Wallach representation $\pi$ of $G$ and every smooth character $\eta$ of $H$.

papers.title: Universally extendible characters
papers.abstract: Let theta be an ordinary character or a Brauer character of a finite group N. We show that theta extends to every overgroup $G=G_\theta\trianglerighteq N$ if and only if Z(N) <= Ker(theta) and the deflated character of Inn(N) extends to Aut(N)_theta. This equivalence is compatible with fields of values. A similar investigation for extensions from subnormal subgroups leads to a new characteristic subgroup of N.

papers.title: Virtual double categories of split two-sided 2-fibrations
papers.abstract: This paper introduces and studies split two-sided 2-fibrations and locally discrete split two-sided 2-fibrations, using a formal categorical approach. We generalise Street's notion of split two-sided fibration internal to a 2-category to one internal to a sesquicategory. Given a sesquicategory we construct a virtual double category whose horizontal (loose) morphisms are its internal split two-sided fibrations. Specialising to the sesquicategory of lax natural transformations, we obtain the virtual double category of split two-sided 2-fibrations, which we study in detail. We then restrict to the sub-virtual double category of locally discrete split two-sided 2-fibrations and show that therein the usual Yoneda 2-functors satisfy a double-categorical formal notion of Yoneda morphism, which formally captures universal properties similar to those satisfied by the morphisms comprising a Yoneda structure on a 2-category. As a consequence we obtain a 'two-sided Grothendieck correspondence' of locally discrete split two-sided 2-fibrations $A \nrightarrow B$ and 2-functors $B \to Cat^{A^{op}}$. Restricting to $A = 1$, the terminal 2-category, we improve Lambert's 'Grothendieck correspondence' for locally discrete split op-2-fibrations by extending the sense in which it is functorial.

papers.title: Weak del Pezzo surfaces are characterized by the existence of $2$-tilting bundles
papers.abstract:
For $d\geq1$, a tilting bundle on a regular proper $d$-dimensional variety over a field is called $d$-tilting if its endomorphism algebra has global dimension $d$, the smallest possible value. We prove that, over any field, the existence of a $d$-tilting bundle implies that the anticanonical bundle is semiample and big, and hence the variety is weak Fano. Moreover, the endomorphism algebra is $d$-representation tame.
  Conversely, every weak del Pezzo surface over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic admits a $2$-tilting bundle. Thus a smooth projective surface over such a field admits a $2$-tilting bundle if and only if it is a weak del Pezzo surface. This proves the variety case of Chan's conjecture, originally formulated in characteristic zero, and extends it to arbitrary characteristic.
  As an application, we construct a non-commutative crepant resolution (NCCR) of the anticanonical ring of any regular proper $d$-dimensional variety over any field admitting a $d$-tilting bundle. The NCCR is the endomorphism algebra of the pulled-back bundle on the total space of the canonical bundle. In particular, we obtain NCCRs of anticanonical cones over Du Val del Pezzo surfaces over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic. These NCCRs are the $3$-Calabi--Yau completions of the endomorphism algebras of $2$-tilting bundles on the minimal resolutions, extending the known construction for smooth del Pezzo surfaces to the Du Val case.
